```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(gapminder)
```

## What is plotly? {auto-animate="true"}

- plotly turns regular graphs into interactive visualizations such as interactive scatterplots, 3D scatterplots, and animated graphs
- plotly works with other R libraries such as ggplot2 to further enhance graphics


## Using plotly to create interactive scatterplots. {auto-animate="true"}

```{.r code-line-numbers="1-4|5-8"}
plot_ly(
  data = penguins,
  x = ~bill_length_mm,
  y = ~flipper_length_mm,
  color = ~species,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers"
)
```

## Using plotly to create interactive scatterplots. {auto-animate="true"}

```{r}

```


## Using ggplot with plotly to create interactive scatterplots. {auto-animate="true"}

```{.r code-line-numbers="1-5|6"}
ggplot_graph <- penguins |>
  ggplot(aes(x = bill_length_mm,
      y = flipper_length_mm,
      color = species)) +
  geom_point()
ggplotly(ggplot_graph)
```

## Using plotly to create interactive histograms. {auto-animate="true"}

```{.r code-line-numbers="1-10|5"}
plot_ly(
  data = penguins,
  x = ~body_mass_g,
  color = ~species,
  type = "histogram",
  opacity = 0.6
) |>
  layout(
    barmode = "overlay"
  )
```

## Using plotly to create 3D scatterplots. {auto-animate="true"}

```{.r code-line-numbers="1-9|7"}
plot_ly(
  data = penguins,
  x = ~bill_length_mm,
  y = ~flipper_length_mm,
  z = ~bill_depth_mm,
  color = ~species,
  type = "scatter3d",
  mode = "markers"
)
```



## Using plotly to create 3D scatterplots. {auto-animate="true"}



## Using plotly to model plots over time. {auto-animate="true"}

```{.r code-line-numbers="1-10|7"}
plot_ly(
  data = gapminder::gapminder,
  x = ~gdpPercap,
  y = ~lifeExp,
  size = ~pop,
  color = ~continent,
  frame = ~year,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers"
)
```

```{r}
)
```


## Using plotly to create interactive maps. {auto-animate="true"}

```{.r code-line-numbers="1-21"}
data("quakes")
plot_ly(
  data = quakes,
  type = "scattermapbox",
  mode = "markers",
  lat = ~lat,
  lon = ~long,
  marker = list(size = 8),
  text = ~paste(
    "Magnitude:", mag,
    "<br>Depth:", depth, "km"
  ),
  hoverinfo = "text"
) |>
  layout(
    mapbox = list(
      style = "open-street-map",
      zoom = 3,
      center = list(lat = -20, lon = 180)
    )
  )
```

## Using plotly to model functions in three dimensions. {auto-animate="true"}

```{.r code-line-numbers="1-6"}
x <- seq(-5, 5, length.out = 50)
y <- seq(-5, 5, length.out = 50)
z <- outer(x, y, function(x, y) x^2 + y^2)

plot_ly(x = x, y = y, z = z) |>
  add_surface()
```



## Using plotly to model functions in three dimensions. {auto-animate="true"}

```{r}
x <- seq(-5, 5, length.out = 50)
y <- seq(-5, 5, length.out = 50)
z <- outer(x, y, function(x, y) x^2 + y^2)

plot_ly(x = x, y = y, z = z) |>
  add_surface()
```


## Using plotly to model stock prices. {auto-animate="true"}

```{.r code-line-numbers="1-16"}
data("EuStockMarkets")
stock_data <- data.frame(
  day = seq_len(nrow(EuStockMarkets)),
  DAX = EuStockMarkets[, "DAX"],
  SMI = EuStockMarkets[, "SMI"],
  CAC = EuStockMarkets[, "CAC"],
  FTSE = EuStockMarkets[, "FTSE"]
)

plot_ly(
  data = stock_data,
  x = ~day) |>
  add_lines(y = ~DAX, name = "DAX") |>
  add_lines(y = ~SMI, name = "SMI") |>
  add_lines(y = ~CAC, name = "CAC") |>
  add_lines(y = ~FTSE, name = "FTSE") |>
  layout(
    title = "European Stock Market Index Values",
    xaxis = list(title = "Trading Day"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Index Value")
  )
```
